question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Y∼N(-2,{4}^{2}),$ compute $P(Y\ge -4.48).$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.7\,$ | $\,0.2420\,$ | $\,0.2389\,$ | $\,0.2358\,$ |
| $\,-0.6\,$ | $\,0.2743\,$ | $\,0.2709\,$ | $\,0.2676\,$ |
| $\,-0.5\,$ | $\,0.3085\,$ | $\,0.3050\,$ | $\,0.3015\,$ |

$P(Y\ge -4.48)=$
{{field-1}}

current_example.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $Y \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2),$ we have

$$
P(Y \geq y) = P \left( Z \geq \dfrac{y-\mu}{\sigma} \right)
$$

where $Z \sim N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu = 5$ and $\sigma = 4.$

First, we transform $Y$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge 2.92) & =P(Z\ge \frac{2.92-5}{4}) \\  & =P(Z\ge -0.52)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14263116/assets/049e4733082674668ebbe2c5a710cd847f1db16d26fdcd2af6e603941efdffe7.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $\Phi(z)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -0.52) & =1-P(Z<-0.52) \\  & =1-P(Z\le -0.52) \\  & =1-Φ(-0.52)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
\Phi(-0.52) =0.3015.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -0.52) & =1-Φ(-0.52) \\  & =1-0.3015 \\  & =0.6985.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(Y \geq 2.92) = 0.6985.
$$
